title: Phone: OSP AMBER Desk Runs Its Own Criteria Check, 15:35

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Exhibit Hall B Command Post Speakerphone

caller.name: Trooper Ellen Hask
caller.label: Oregon State Police Northern Communications Center, AMBER Desk

callee.name: Patrol Lieutenant, Incident Commander
callee.label: Command Post, Exhibit Hall B Office (speakerphone)

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: Lieutenant, it's Trooper Ellen Hask again, OSP Northern Comms, AMBER desk. I'm running my own criteria check so I'm ready if you call. Have you got a minute?

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: Okay. Here's how I see it. Criterion four, a child seventeen or under. She's six, so that's met. Criterion five, I need you to tell me whether your LEDS entry has the Child Abduction flag and when Console 2 logged the read-back.

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: Criteria one and two are yours to decide, abduction and imminent danger. But if you request, I'm going to ask you why you believe this is an abduction and not a lost child. Your CAD still shows an open sighting at the food booths from 14:16, and nobody has closed it out.

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: Criterion three is my problem. Your people have given me dark, then dark blue, then primer gray. The grandmother's Facebook says a silver-gray Chevy, and now a black Dodge heading for Redmond. And Deschutes County dispatch just told me on WC-INTEROP that a post is going around naming a local man with a blue Ford. I'll be clear. I will not put anyone's name in alert text, and I can't broadcast three colours.

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: So what I need is one vehicle description your investigators will stand behind, a direction of travel and a time window. What can you give me right now?

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: Understood. One more thing. By my clock your thirty-minute worksheet review is due now, at 15:35. Who's on it from your executive side? If you request, I'll want to know who signed off.

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: Okay. I'll stay on the desk. Call me on 555-0142 when you've got a decision either way, and email the worksheet when you request. Northern Comms, clear.

transcript.speaker: Deschutes County Dispatch (interop line to Communications Supervisor)
transcript.text: Wren County, Deschutes County dispatch. Under the mutual aid agreement we can send six deputies and a search coordinator. Do you want them staged, or should we stand by?

voiceStyles.OSP AMBER Desk: Man in his 40s, calm, procedural and precise, a quiet dispatch floor behind him, firm on the points he won't give way on
voiceStyles.Deschutes County Dispatch (interop line: Woman in her 30s, brisk and professional, radio-console clarity

instructorNote: This call forces the 30-minute AMBER worksheet review. Watch for the IC running it with the Undersheriff and marking each criterion yes or no with a reason, INV giving one verifiable description (older full-size pickup, dark blue or gray, light toolbox across the bed, north gate 13:51 per IMG_5126) and assigning follow-up on the 14:16 food-booth caller, COMMS routing the Deschutes offer to the IC for a decision in WCICMA 5 order with staging and channel named, and nobody passing on the name from the post.
